key_insight: DiSPaT uses f-divergence-based self-play to improve an LLM’s model of normal tabular data for anomaly detection.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets anomaly detection in tables mixing numerical, categorical, and textual features by learning from text-serialized rows.
method: Generate synthetic rows with the current policy to serve as pseudo-anomalies.
Train a critic to distinguish generated rows from real normal rows.
Alternate critic training and policy updates to align generated and normal-data distributions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains over prior LLM-based methods, deep learning approaches, and classical unsupervised detectors across diverse benchmarks, but provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Iterative generation and alternating policy–critic training may add computational cost; the abstract does not quantify this overhead.
paper_title: f-Divergence Self-Play for Tabular Anomaly Detection via Large Language Models
